1 │ # Turning attrs objects into tuples is slower than it needs to be
   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ When I turn an attrs object into a tuple, each value in it is put through a long
   5 │ chain of checks. Plain values such as numbers and text cannot match most of
   6 │ those checks, so the effort is wasted. The other helper that turns an object
   7 │ into a dictionary already passes over plain values early and leaves them alone,
   8 │ but the helper that builds a tuple does not.
   9 │ 
  10 │ ## What should happen
  11 │ Plain values should be noticed straight away and skipped past the extra checks,
  12 │ so the same tuple comes back faster. The values, their order, and their types
  13 │ should stay just as they are today.
  14 │ 
  15 │ ## About this project
  16 │ attrs is a small helper library for Python. It lets people write short classes
  17 │ that hold data, without repeating the same setup code again and again. One of
  18 │ its helpers turns such an object into a tuple of its values.
  19 │ 
  20 │ ## Problem this solves
  21 │ People who turn many objects, or objects with many fields, into tuples wait
  22 │ longer than needed for a result they already know how to get. A common habit is
  23 │ to run that conversion in a loop, so the wasted effort adds up.
  24 │ 
  25 │ ## What changed
  26 │ The tuple helper now spots plain values early, the same way the dictionary
  27 │ helper already does. Values, their order, and their types come back the same.
  28 │ The choices for how collections are handled behave the same as before. What
  29 │ goes up is the speed of the conversion.
  30 │ 
  31 │ ## Impact
  32 │ Speed, with no change to the result.
  33 │ 
  34 │ ## User experience
  35 │ Before, a loop that builds tuples from thousands of objects takes a while, and
  36 │ there is no way to make it quicker. After, the same loop finishes sooner, and
  37 │ every tuple it hands back is the same as before.
  38 │

---
== changelog.d/1427.change.md
Values passed to the `__init__()` method of `attrs` classes are now correctly passed to `__attrs_pre_init__()` instead of their default values (in cases where *kw_only* was not specified).

== changelog.d/1446.change.md
Added support for Python 3.14 and [PEP 749](https://peps.python.org/pep-0749/).

== changelog.d/1448.change.md
`attrs.validators.deep_mapping()` now allows to leave out either *key_validator* xor *value_validator*.

== changelog.d/1449.change.md
`attrs.validators.deep_iterator()` and `attrs.validators.deep_mapping()` now accept lists and tuples for all validators and wrap them into a `attrs.validators.and_()`.

== changelog.d/1451.change.md
Added support for Python 3.14 and [PEP 749](https://peps.python.org/pep-0749/).

== changelog.d/1457.breaking.md
Class-level `kw_only=True` behavior is now consistent with `dataclasses`.

Previously, a class that sets `kw_only=True` makes all attributes keyword-only, including those from base classes.
If an attribute sets `kw_only=False`, that setting is ignored, and it is still made keyword-only.

Now, only the attributes defined in that class that doesn't explicitly set `kw_only=False` are made keyword-onl
== changelog.d/1461.change.md
Fixed annotations for `attrs.field(converter=...)`.
Previously, a `tuple` of converters was only accepted if it had exactly one element.

== changelog.d/1463.change.md
The performance of `attrs.asdict()` has been improved by 45–260%.
